clue.text: Gold coin — a sovereign? — in circulation

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit
a sovereign is a pound coin, and L is the abbreviation for pound (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a gold coin doing the rounds might be a sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British gold coin worth one pound, which is how it gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something orbital goes round and round on a circular path, as a satellite does.

clue.text: Nothing to fix at home birth

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
to rig is to fix dishonestly
in means at home

explanation.surface: An arranged home birth leaves nothing to fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Origin means beginning or descent, the point where something is born.

clue.text: Transport for bicentenarian's dog

definitions.meaning: The ship that carried Darwin round the world
a small hound used in hunting hares

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both Darwin's survey ship and a breed of hunting hound.

clue.text: Bicentenarian's end was a century in the first test

parts.note: taken as written
A is the first letter, as in grade A

indicators.note: in places the century inside the test

parts.note: a trial is a test
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A cricketer scores a hundred in the first Test match of the series.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre in 1865, so his end was dramatic in the stage sense. The surface's century and Test are cricket terms: a hundred runs, and an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln died after being shot in a playhouse, so his death was fittingly stage-related, an apt cryptic description.

clue.text: Hands holding long drink

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps the other inside it

parts.note: the left and right hands give L and R
an age is a long time, so it can stand for long

explanation.surface: Two hands hold a tall glass of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a common drink.

clue.text: City concealed by 20 of homo sapiens, say

indicators.note: something concealed by another is wrapped up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: 20 down's answer is a word for representatives, and agents in the secret sense are spies
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A city lies hidden among undercover operatives, in a clue about the human race.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'City' is the City of London, the financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Homo sapiens is an example of a biological kind, the human one; 'of' is part of the definition phrase, as in the title of Darwin's book.

clue.text: See 27
With telepathy you begin to observe

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, includes telepathy
Y is a text-speak short form of you

explanation.surface: A mind-reader tells you that you will start to see things.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, which is to start seeing something.

clue.text: Just one card (not a spade) in the Yorkshire Dales

indicators.note: not means the named piece is left out

parts.note: in card games a singleton is the only card held in a suit
S is short for spades in bridge notation

explanation.surface: A card player holds one card, not a spade, while in the Dales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are hill country in northern England; Ingleton is a village there known for its waterfalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingleton is a village located in this national park, so the phrase describes where it is.

clue.text: Support leader writers in use of tenterhooks?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
in places the writers inside the use

parts.note: taken as written
pens are writing implements

explanation.surface: A newspaper's leader writers rely on keeping readers on tenterhooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support leader writers' reads as a newspaper's editorial staff, but 'leader' only takes the first letter of 'Support'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on tenterhooks is to be in a state of anxious uncertainty, which is what suspense means.

clue.text: Cross, first class

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one, the first number
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone is cross at being called first class.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate and cross both describe a person who is angry.

clue.text: Islands associated with bicentenarian celebration at a lot of temples

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration

indicators.note: a lot of the word, not all of it, means some letters are dropped here

parts.note: pagodas are tiered temples of East Asia

explanation.surface: A party at a set of temples marks the anniversary of a famous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle marks the 200th birthdays of Darwin and Lincoln, both born on 12 February 1809. Taking DA from the middle of PAGODAS leaves PAGOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin's visit to these Pacific islands shaped his theory of evolution, so they are linked with him.

clue.text: It gains point in lyrical composition from lack of letters

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the rearranged letters
a composition puts its material together in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered
gains means the next piece is added on

parts.note: taken as written
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A poem gains a point, apparently from someone who cannot write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges LYRICAL into ILLRACY, and 'in' puts ITE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiteracy is the inability to read or write, a want of reading and writing skill.

clue.text: Just water

definitions.meaning: ... means only, as in a ... child

explanation.definitionFit: Mere is both an adjective meaning simply or only and a noun for a lake.

clue.text: Broken by nasty sequel, old lady is mocked

indicators.note: a piece broken by another is split open with the other inside

parts.note: burd is an old word for a lady or maiden

indicators.note: nasty suggests the word is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An old woman is ridiculed after a nasty follow-up story.
explanation.walkthrough: Burd is an archaic, chiefly Scots, word for a lady, rarely seen outside crosswords; 'nasty' and 'Broken by' are the working signals, not part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To burlesque something is to parody it, so burlesqued means mocked by imitation.

clue.text: February 1: Teachers for starters

parts.note: the puzzle appeared in February, and INST (instant) is the old commercial abbreviation for this month
I is the Roman numeral one
tutors are teachers

explanation.surface: A diary entry for 1 February lists teachers to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: INST, short for instant, meant 'of the current month' in old business letters; the clue ran in February, so the month itself stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Institutors are those who institute or found things, people who start them off.

clue.text: Geri, possibly, in other clips

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might form something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Geri Halliwell appears in some other video clips.
explanation.walkthrough: Geri Halliwell was Ginger in the 1990s pop group, so the whole clue both defines and builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Geri Halliwell was a member of the band, so she is an example of one.

clue.text: 1 down of bicentenarian given gab with his large heart?

indicators.note: given here means the letters are offered up to be worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a large heart is the whole inside of the word, all but its first and last letters

parts.note: his refers to the bicentenarian, Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A great-hearted man is credited with the gift of the gab and a humble home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large heart' leaves INCOL from LINCOLN, and with GAB it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln was born in a log cabin in Kentucky, so that was his origin.

clue.text: Bother about comeback of what bicentenarian was and wasn't

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: drat is a mild curse like bother
read as come back, the word come turned around

explanation.surface: Someone curses the return of what a statesman both was and was not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' splits as come plus back, giving EMOC. Lincoln was a democrat in belief but a Republican, not a Democrat, by party.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln championed government by the people, yet belonged to the rival Republican Party.

clue.text: Hospital-wise 3 is go

definitions.meaning: 3 down is a word about the stage; in hospital terms the theatre is the operating theatre, so its adjective is the surgical one
go, as in all systems go, means working and ready

explanation.definitionFit: Operational means in working order, and also relates to surgical operations as done in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Not many say Scrabble letter is pointless

indicators.note: say means a word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: few means not many
Scrabble letters come on tiles

explanation.surface: A player says few Scrabble letters are worth anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile means useless, achieving nothing.

clue.text: Reps need a loo

parts.note: Gents is a men's lavatory, the loo

explanation.surface: Sales representatives need a toilet break.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the Gents' is the usual name for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Reps, short for representatives, act on someone's behalf, as agents do.

clue.text: Pen for shared work?

parts.note: the prefix co- means together or shared, as in co-owner
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone wants a pen for a joint project.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop is a pen or cage for poultry.

clue.text: What bicentenarian said of museum man — "citizen eating snake without its tail"

parts.note: J Paul Getty founded the Getty Museum; the possessive gives GETTYS

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a burgess is a citizen of a borough

indicators.note: a tail dropped means the snake loses a letter

parts.note: an adder is a snake

explanation.surface: A famous speaker remarks of a museum founder that a citizen is swallowing a truncated snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln, the other bicentenarian, spoke at Gettysburg in 1863. Strictly, losing a tail should cost the snake its final letter, but the setter drops the E instead; 'eating' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln's famous speech of 1863 is known by the town where he gave it, so it is literally what he said.

clue.text: Amicable island game has me dropped after century

indicators.note: after puts this piece second, behind the century

parts.note: a ton is a hundred

indicators.note: dropped means the named part is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friendly island game, I am left out after scoring a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonga was named the Friendly Islands by Captain Cook, hence 'Amicable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga's old nickname is the Friendly Islands, so it is a friendly island nation.

clue.text: Duet for piano with melody

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, soft
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A duet for piano carries a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two together, as a duet is two performers.

clue.text: Lawyers — with one exception — have an uncivilised character

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers
bar means except, so it stands for an exception
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lawyers, bar one, are said to be boorish.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbarian is a savage or uncultured person, someone lacking refinement.

clue.text: What bicentenarian fought for hurt foot, not head

indicators.note: not head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot

explanation.surface: An old soldier went to war despite a sore foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln led the North, the Union, in the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln fought the Civil War to preserve the federal United States against secession.

clue.text: Obvious choice for bicentenarian as to the 1 down of 5 across

definitions.text: for bicentenarian as to the 1 down of 5 across
definitions.meaning: Darwin's explanation of how species arise, the subject of his book on the origin of species

explanation.definitionFit: Darwin's term for evolution by survival of the fittest also reads as a plain phrase for the expected pick.

clue.text: See 22
